subject: Visibility review: private deployment module dependency tree and CI telemetry
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Visibility review: private deployment module dependency tree and CI telemetry

Hi Marissa / Jonas —

I sketched a dependency tree for the private-deploy modules (Terraform modules, Helm charts, and the Ansible bootstraps) and attached a quick SVG. The goal is to get a short pass from Product and Platform on two things before we land the change into the main pipeline: 1) do we have the right gating points in CI to avoid partial deploys, and 2) are we collecting sufficient telemetry to prove safe rollbacks (so Security can sign off).

Specifically asking for:
- Confirm owners for the four leaf modules in the diagram and whether anyone needs to be added to codeowners for release gating.
- Approve the proposed CI checkpoints in the attached gitlab-ci-telemetry-snippet.yml (unit, manifest lint, plan-check, canary-deploy, telemetry-bake) — we want to make the canary window and telemetry metrics explicit.
- Any red flags for on-prem customers (e.g., networking changes that require a hardware maintenance window).

Attachments: module-dep-tree.svg (visual), gitlab-ci-telemetry-snippet.yml (pipeline diff), iac-change-matrix.xlsx (impact matrix).

I kept this deliberately short — if useful I can run a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility review: private deployment module dependency tree and CI telemetry

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick notes inline so we have a record: 

- Owners: I think the leaf modules map to: 
  - priv-networking -> Olga (networking team) — need to confirm ownership; will loop her in if required.
  - priv-kms -> Jonas (security) — tagging as primary and backup.
  - priv-orch -> SRE (ownership is split; we should add a steward role).
  - priv-init -> Platform tools (Tessa) — Tessa should approve the Ansible bootstrap step.

- CI checkpoints: the plan-check is ok but add an explicit terraform state-lock verification step before apply. Also the canary window needs two explicit metrics: token latency (p50/p95) and KV-cache miss rate. If telemetry doesn't show regressions for 30 minutes we can promote.

- On-prem risk: any BGP or LACP changes need a maintenance window. If priv-networking contains eBPF tweaks, we should mark that as high-risk and require a manual approval gate (not automated).

Can you paste the snippet for the state-lock step? I can add wording for the security evidence pack. If you're planning a walkthrough tomorrow, 10:30–11:00 PT works.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Partner Deployments
Redwood Inference

Cc: acme-ops <eng@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility review: private deployment module dependency tree and CI telemetry

Thanks for the diagram — Bethany from Acme here. A couple notes from our infra team: 

- We appreciate the telemetry focus. For our side the key requirement is a rollback signal that does not rely on external metrics (we need a locally-observed health check). Can you add a small health probe that checks a local inference worker responding to a lightweight prompt?
- Regarding canaries: our policy requires canary traffic to be forced-by-header for 30 minutes before a wider roll. Please keep the canary toggle in the Helm values so we can flip it from our control plane.
- Attachments: we cannot accept outbound access during the first canary by default; is there wg-bypass for artifact fetches? We'll need an offline artifact mirror.

We can join the walkthrough at 10:30 PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Bethany Liu
Director, Cloud Operations
Acme Cloud
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: bethany.liu@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility review: private deployment module dependency tree and CI telemetry

Nice responses — thanks all. Quick synthesis and next steps so the ticket can move: 

1) Owners and codeowners: Dylan, please confirm final owners for the diagram. Marissa, please start a PR to add stewards/codeowners for priv-orch and priv-init. Deadline: EOD Wed 2027-05-26.

2) CI changes: Dylan to add state-lock verification and the two telemetry metrics to the gitlab snippet. Use explicit job names: tf-state-lock-check, telemetry-smoke (p50/p95 latency, kv_miss_rate). Add a manual approval job named manual-onprem-approval that triggers for high-risk modules.

3) On-prem controls: Bethany's requests accepted — add a local health-check endpoint in the Helm chart (values: localProbe.enabled=true) and document artifact mirror instructions in the iac-change-matrix.xlsx. Add a feature-flag gate (helm value) to control canary-by-header.

4) Rollback playbook: Create a short runbook (one page) showing the exact commands for forced rollback and the telemetry checks to run. We should store the runbook in the private drive link above and reference it in the pipeline job.

5) Walkthrough: 10:30–11:00 PT tomorrow — please bring the SVG and pipeline snippet. I'll chair and record the session; action owners should be present.

I'll open a JIRA ticket PRIVDEP-817 and assign owners after we confirm. If there are gating legal/security items, escalate to Security-COMPLIANCE.

Jonas Weber
VP, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
